newsitem.title: ITALY: Prodi sees lira devaluation if Italy misses EMU.
newsitem.headline: Prodi sees lira devaluation if Italy misses EMU.

text.p: Prime Minister Romano Prodi on Tuesday forecast a speculative "assault on the lira" and the currency's devaluation if Italy fails to join Europe's planned currency union from the beginning in 1999.

In a television interview, Prodi also sought to calm a heated political debate on the future of the state pensions system, saying reform required careful thought and should not be rushed. Reduced spending on pensions and other welfare benefits are widely regarded as vital to Italy's bid to meet and sustain the criteria for membership of European economic and monetary union (EMU) from the outset.

"I am convinced that, if we don't enter Europe in the first leg, all hell will break loose in the first year. There will be an assault on the lira, devaluation (and) inflation will take off again," Prodi said.
European Union countries that want to join EMU from January 1, 1999 will be judged early next year on the basis of their 1997 accounts.
A key criterion is whether or not the public sector deficit is within three percent of gross domestic product, a target Italy is straining to meet.
Prodi's centre-left coalition has faced strains over the objectives because of the perceived need to cut welfare spending, particularly on Italy's generous pensions system.
"Pensions are such an important part of our life that we must enact reforms after a great deal of thought," Prodi said.
He said any change to the system had to be brought about through agreement with trades unions and political parties on the basis of hard data.
Prodi has mandated a special commission to investigate welfare spending and expected it to present its findings early next month.
